patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a prominent search field in the header area: a full-width input near the top on mobile and a long horizontal search box in the desktop masthead.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should support text entry and search submission; likely also supports live suggestions/autocomplete because of its prominence and placement in global navigation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show autocomplete results or a submit button, so live results are implied rather than certain.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Desktop header shows multiple compact nav items aligned to the right of the search field, consistent with top-level navigation labels that likely reveal submenus.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Top-level nav items should open submenus on click/hover and close on outside interaction or escape; active/open state should be visually indicated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw submenu panels, so this is inferred from the multi-item desktop nav structure and common responsive behavior.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Mobile sketch has a simplified stacked layout with no visible full horizontal nav, implying collapsed navigation for small screens.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A menu toggle should reveal/hide the primary navigation in an overlay or expandable panel; likely needed because desktop-style nav links are absent in the mobile header.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit hamburger icon is drawn, so the exact trigger style and whether it opens a drawer, sheet, or accordion menu is unclear.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Near the top content area in both sketches there is a horizontal row of small adjacent rectangular items beneath the title/meta region, visually matching tabs for switching sections.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Selecting a tab should swap the visible content panel without full page reload, maintain an active state, and support keyboard navigation between tabs.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether all tabs swap inline panels or some may navigate to anchored sections/pages.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include image galleries: a main cover/media area with adjacent small selectors and a row/grid of screenshot thumbnails, which strongly implies click-to-enlarge media viewing.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Clicking cover art or screenshots should likely open a larger overlay/lightbox with focus trap, close controls, and possibly previous/next navigation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly depict an overlay, so enlargement could alternatively navigate to a dedicated media page instead of a modal.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a long vertically stacked page with repeated content blocks and a constrained screenshot grid, suggesting truncated sections that may expand or reveal more items progressively on small screens.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Could expose additional screenshots, metadata, or long lists via a 'more' control to avoid overwhelming the mobile layout.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit button is drawn; this may instead be simple full-page scrolling with no incremental loading.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile layout compresses many metadata groups and content sections into stacked blocks, which commonly become collapsible disclosures on small screens to save space.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Section headers could expand/collapse details such as credits, identifiers, reviews, or contribution info.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No chevrons or explicit disclosure markers are visible, so this remains speculative.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a content-heavy responsive detail page with modest but important JavaScript needs. Core shared behaviors are global search, tabbed section switching, and media enlargement from cover/screenshot areas. The main cross-viewport difference is navigation: desktop likely uses exposed top-nav items with dropdowns, while mobile likely collapses navigation behind a menu trigger. Mobile may also compress long sections into disclosures or progressive reveal patterns, but those are less explicit than the search, tabs, and media interactions.
